questions: Did the facial weakness or drooping begin suddenly, within the last 24 hours?
Do you have weakness or numbness in an arm or leg on either side?
Have you had trouble speaking, understanding speech, walking, or keeping your balance?
Is one side of your face newly unable to smile normally?
Is the forehead on the affected side also weak or unable to wrinkle?
Are you unable to completely close the affected eye?
Do you have new double vision or loss of vision?
Is one pupil noticeably larger than the other?
Do you have a severe or unusual headache?
Do you have eye pain, severe redness, or marked sensitivity to light?
Have you had pain around the ear or behind the ear on the affected side?
Have you noticed blisters or a rash in or around that ear or on the face?
Have you recently had a cold, fever, COVID-19, or another infection?
Have you had any recent head injury, eye injury, or surgery?
Have you previously had similar facial weakness?

results: 1. Measure visual acuity in each eye separately.
visual acuity and colour vision: normal
2. Perform slit-lamp examination of the cornea, conjunctiva, anterior chamber, and eyelids.
3. Perform fluorescein staining with cobalt-blue illumination.
4. Measure intraocular pressure in both eyes.
pupil examination (size, light reaction): equal and reactive
ocular motility examination: failure to adduct the right eye
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Right oculomotor (III) nerve palsy, most consistent with post-infectious inflammatory neuritis

ALTERNATIVE: Right medial rectus muscle/orbital myositis

ALTERNATIVE: Demyelinating brainstem lesion causing right internuclear ophthalmoplegia

ALTERNATIVE: Compressive right oculomotor nerve lesion (including posterior communicating artery aneurysm)
order_raw:
1. Measure visual acuity in each eye separately.
2. Perform slit-lamp examination of the cornea, conjunctiva, anterior chamber, and eyelids.
3. Perform fluorescein staining with cobalt-blue illumination.
4. Measure intraocular pressure in both eyes.
5. Examine pupils and extraocular movements.
6. Perform a dilated funduscopic examination.
dx: Right oculomotor (III) nerve palsy, most consistent with post-infectious inflammatory neuritis
